newsitem.title: THAILAND: Foreign brokers oppose Thai agent fee limit.
newsitem.headline: Foreign brokers oppose Thai agent fee limit.

text.p: Foreign stock brokers appealed to the Thai Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for help in scrapping Thailand's 40 percent broking agent fees limit.

Foreign brokers, led by George Morgan who is country manager of HG Asia, told SEC chief Pakorn Malakul na Ayudhya on Tuesday that Thailand's attempts to regulate their offshore business ran counter to a national policy aimed at liberalising and developing its capital market.

"Attempts to bring offshore trading onshore before the SET is ready to welcome foreign members are liable to backfire. Bringing offshore trading onshore would sharply reduce foreign brokers' profitability," he said in a statement on Wednesday.
Morgan said Thailand was trailing South Korea and Taiwan in granting full market membership to foreign brokers and in licensing wholly foreign owned broking branches.
He said Thailand's 40 percent limit on foreign share sale agent fee was below a 50 percent rate that foreign brokers obtained before the government put a cap on it this year.

Foreign brokers described the agent fee limit as protectionist, saying it would retard development of Bangkok as a regional financial centre as it gives Thai brokers a share of offshore trading business without doing anything to earn it.
